content_of_post_to_comment:
So I'm at this point where I'm somewhat torn. I got out of a long relationship that was particularly traumatic almost two years ago and havent really put myself out there

In my head, I have rationalized not pursuing women by saying that I am happy alone. My general mindset is that while I know that there are lots of good women, I'm just not at the point where my brain can visualize the reward enough to deal with the effort required to find them.

I think it is a motivation issue. I recently quit porn, and this only seems like half the battle. It feels like it lights more of a fire to talk to them, but it's purely from a place of horniness. It doesn't solve the issue of trust nor the innate paranoia that a woman will only want me for what I can do for her.

The problem is that yes, healing has done an amazing job of making me confident of my own intentions and self-respect. I don't fear being tricked or having my heart broken because I allowed my insecurities to blind myself to someone's red flags. It's more that most people are selfish, and therefore I'm going to meet a lot of women who suck. Without the unhealthy “void fill” that drove me to seek relationships in the past, I just can't visualize the benefit of wasting my time in order to be dissapointed so often.

So I guess here's my question: Am i overthinking it? Am I just supposed to starve myself of sex dopamine (quit porn) for long enough that I'm driven to talk to a few women? Does the rest just work itself out?
comment: Quitting porn might remove some noise, but I wouldn't make horniness the engine for dating. You don't need to convince yourself that women are worth the effort or assume most will disappoint you. Maybe just start meeting people with no goal beyond seeing who you actually enjoy being around. Trust can be earned slowly instead of solved in advance.
